_doc: Accepted survivors for scripts/local-ci/guard-ablation.mjs (M-5a/A2).
A SURVIVOR is a mutation of a validator's execute() that leaves every fixture in
its pack producing the same frozen `expected` — i.e. the rule it touched is pinned
by nothing. A new survivor is a HARD CI FAILURE: it means a rule shipped without a
fixture that fails when the rule is reverted alone.
This list may only SHRINK. Two rules, both enforced by the tool:
1. a survivor absent from `accepted` fails the gate;
2. an `accepted` entry that is no longer a survivor ALSO fails the gate, so a
stale exemption cannot outlive the gap it excused. Delete it in the same
commit that kills the mutant.
Every entry must carry `reason` and `class`. `class: equivalent` means the mutation
provably cannot change behaviour. `class: unpinned` means the rule genuinely lacks a
fixture and MUST carry an `owner` naming the work package that closes it.
Scope note: the CLI wrapper at the foot of each validator is NOT mutated.
The parity fixtures call execute() directly via exec-one.js and never invoke the
CLI, so they pin no wrapper line by construction — the first run of this tool
reported nine survivors and all nine were wrapper guards. The wrapper is pinned
instead by parity/cli-contract/run-tests.js (all four exit-3 paths and both input
modes, per validator) and by scripts/local-ci/cli-block-lint.mjs (the nine copies
cannot drift). See the header of guard-ablation.mjs.

why_narrow: These are the three packs SC-9 modifies, and two operators are enough to
reproduce the failure this mechanism exists to catch. Extending to the other six
validators and to the wider operator catalogue (guard-on, boundary flips,
constant offsets, negation, dropped pushes) is M-5b/B6's decision, to be made on
measured mutant counts and runtime rather than on estimates.

note: Measured on this checkout, not projected. M-5a measured 18 mutants / 122 calls / 6 ms
over the same three packs before SC-9 enlarged them; SC-9 roughly doubled both the rule
count and the fixture count for ~2x the cost, still an order of magnitude under the
~5 s parity step. Recorded so M-5b/B6 extrapolates from data: ~12 mutants and ~4 ms per
SC-9 is also the first evidence that this mechanism earns its place. It went RED on
SC-9's own first cut, naming four rules the new fixtures did not pin: the empty-prefix
branch of underPrefix, both absolute-path guards, and the malformed-entry count. Three
were closed with fixtures. The fourth -- an explicit startsWith('/') test -- turned out
to be dead code, since '/etc/passwd' splits to ['','etc','passwd'] and the empty-segment
rule already rejected it; it was deleted rather than exempted.
